findings: New raw lines 5–19 retain guide identity and replace the detailed May Checkout and Elements bodies with five navigation targets. Checkout remains, Elements is split explicitly into Checkout Sessions and Payment Intents API, and iOS / Android are new routes relative to this pair. Old raw lines 8–10 and 135–141 held the two old headings, with PaymentIntents steps at 156–200. Diff lines 7–12 and 641–647 establish a navigation delta. No linked variant body is present.

Current source lines 13, 19–25 portray two paths and give broadly worded descriptor and DE/GB limits. Qualify that these are the two old full bodies and log all five November links. Descriptor is an explicit instruction in the May manual Checkout route (old raw lines 14–18, 41–49 and 51–112); the May manual Elements PaymentIntent example contains none (old raw lines 180–196). Avoid a universal requirement, unverified uniqueness, or unsupported Direct API feature prohibition based on a missing guide entry.

Current source lines 25, 31 and 33 omit material qualifications: the May Checkout compatibility table says business locations DE/GB and EUR/GBP, nearby private-preview sentence names France/Germany/Ireland, and manual steps and examples use GBP (old raw lines 20–49, 51–112). Keep customer/bank geography, merchant country, currency and preview separate. Refund generally arrives by next business day with up to seven days to appear successful and this guide says no dispute process (old raw lines 125–127 and 632–634). The Elements Dashboard example mentions Swish and USD, both inconsistent with the corresponding Pay by Bank-specific guidance (old raw lines 12, 24–26, 156–196).

The Stripe index lines 353–354 and real-time payments concept lines 18, 89–101 and 217–218 repeat unqualified method and path shorthand. Link dated explanations with reciprocal scope rather than treating navigation as new API behavior.
historical_claims_to_preserve: May 6, 2026 guide describes single-use `pay_by_bank`, customer bank-app or web-portal authentication and redirect back; Checkout is payment mode only, needs one-time and same-currency line items, and distinguishes dynamic presentation from manual listing and a customer statement descriptor. Hosted example uses `success_url`, full embedded `ui_mode: embedded_page` uses `return_url` (old raw lines 12–112).

May's Elements PaymentIntents route prices and creates the PaymentIntent on a trusted server, then passes the customer-scoped client secret to the payment UI. Stripe.js Dahlia is a dated example, live use calls for HTTPS and nested frames carry redirect cautions. Client `stripe.confirmPayment` uses `return_url`, then the return flow retrieves Intent status and distinguishes `succeeded`, `processing` and `requires_payment_method` (old raw lines 156–200, 269–318, 419–450 and 515–569). Preserve guidance against exposing or logging secrets and distinguish Stripe-appended return parameters from merchant embedding a client secret.

Keep Checkout sandbox authorize/authentication failure examples and dated refund period, generally next-business-day arrival, up to seven days to show success and no dispute process in this guide. No test selection or browser return proves payment success, and status is distinct from merchant payout and refund outcome (old raw lines 118–127, 515–569, 632–634).
conflicts: May compatibility EUR/GBP versus manual GBP instructions (old raw lines 20–49), plus DE/GB business location versus the France/Germany/Ireland preview statement, must be quoted in scope. The separate May product overview identifies its preview as customer availability (raw/stripe-pay-by-bank-2025.md:14–22 and 54–62). November product overview separately dates Finland/Ireland/UK customer bank accounts generally available and Belgium/France/Germany private preview, with UK GBP and listed European countries EUR (raw/stripe-payments-pay-by-bank-2026-11-07.md:15–27 and 111–117). None settles current Checkout variant or merchant eligibility.

May Elements Dashboard Swish and USD example (old raw lines 160–178) conflict with product identity and EUR/GBP guidance (old raw lines 12, 24–26, 139–141 and 180–196). Current source line 33 should warn about both, without silently translating the inconsistent example into supported setup.

Real-time payments concept lines 18 and 99 and product summary line 31 retain mobile unsupported. The May real-time matrix marked Mobile Payment Element unsupported while November marks supported (raw/stripe-real-time-payments-2025.md:24–26 and raw/stripe-payments-real-time-2026-11-07.md:25–27). Those dated capability cells are independent from the five integration links, which give no SDK, supported mobile configuration, or eligibility. Link the distinction reciprocally when reporting mobile support.

Separate November method overview documents a private-preview Elements/PaymentIntents flow combining an initial Pay by Bank payment with a Bacs Direct Debit mandate (raw/stripe-payments-pay-by-bank-2026-11-07.md:264–277). Preserve May's single-use capture and Checkout mode restrictions, do not infer recurring use of the original one-off method or automatic subscription support, and date the overview separately from this index.
unresolved_questions: The November linked variant bodies were not captured. Their actual prerequisites and behavior remain unverified for this page. The May contradictory examples cannot establish a general supported configuration.

findings: Summarize all five November navigation links and label the two detailed May routes as historical. Scope the descriptor to the May manual Checkout flow, restore same-currency one-time and mode constraints, and document the browser-return/status distinction and refund qualification.
conflicts: Current lines 13, 20–25 and 31–33 generalize descriptor, geography and refund timing while omitting the conflicting USD and GBP example scopes (old raw lines 20–49, 125–127 and 156–196). The current index and concept shorthand also need dated route context.
source_assessments.reason: The raw semantic disposition is navigation-only; an independent correction is warranted because the baseline summary can direct an Elements integrator to a Checkout-only instruction, misstate preview geography and hide explicit currency inconsistency.

answers.Q1: The November 7, 2026 capture of https://docs.stripe.com/payments/pay-by-bank/accept-a-payment lists Checkout, Elements with Checkout Sessions or Payment Intents API, plus iOS and Android (new raw lines 5-19). Those links establish documentation routes. The May 6, 2026 guide covers single-use, bank-authenticated redirect payments through Checkout and web Elements PaymentIntents. Checkout lists payment mode, same-currency single-purchase line items, DE/GB business locations and EUR/GBP, with a GBP-specific manual instruction. Manual Checkout sets `pay_by_bank` and a statement descriptor, with `success_url` in hosted and `return_url` in full embedded examples (old raw lines 12-112). Web Elements uses a server-priced PaymentIntent, client-secret handoff, client `confirmPayment` with `return_url`, and PaymentIntent status retrieval for success, pending processing or failure. Browser return alone does not establish a paid payment or available funds (old raw lines 156-200, old raw lines 419-450 and old raw lines 515-569). source-stripe-pay-by-bank-accept-payment.md summarizes the May routes but generalizes the descriptor and geography and lacks the November navigation leaves.
answers.Q2: For https://docs.stripe.com/payments/pay-by-bank/accept-a-payment, the November replacement is a navigation change, including an explicit Elements API split and two mobile links (new raw lines 9-19 versus old raw lines 8-10, old raw lines 135-141 and old raw lines 156-196). The index establishes no SDK contract, current eligibility, or substantive API change. Keep May's one-time Checkout eligibility, manual Checkout statement descriptor, UI-specific return fields, server/client and status boundaries, test steps, and qualified refund timing dated in source-stripe-pay-by-bank-accept-payment.md (old raw lines 20-127, old raw lines 156-200, old raw lines 269-318, old raw lines 515-569 and old raw lines 632-634). Maintain reciprocal warnings for the May compatibility table versus GBP-only instruction, DE/GB business versus France/Germany/Ireland preview wording, and the inconsistent Swish and USD Dashboard example (old raw lines 20-49 and old raw lines 160-196). The separate real-time product matrix's dated mobile-support change and method overview's Bacs-backed recurring private preview have their own evidence. Neither is established by the index, and the distinct preview does not change May Checkout subscription mode.
